items.content:
뉴욕주립 빙엄턴대학 연구진 "CF 두 글자 추가로 변경된 계획 실행"

컴퓨팅 입력 :2026/10/24 09:17 수정: 2026/10/24 09:46

오픈AI 챗GPT, 제미나이, 클로드 등 대규모 언어모델(LLM)의 보안 취약점을 악용하면 로봇이 위험한 행동을 하도록 유도할 수 있다는 연구 결과가 나왔다.

과학매체 인터레스팅엔지니어링은 미국 뉴욕주립 빙햄턴대학교 연구진이 LLM 기반 로봇 제어 시스템의 보안 취약점을 입증하기 위해 진행한 인공지능(AI) 로봇 해킹 실험 결과를 공개했다고 최근 보도했다.

연구진은 LLM에 악의적으로 심어 놓은 숨겨진 트리거 단어가 로봇을 기존 작업 계획에서 벗어나 위험한 행동을 하도록 유도할 수 있다는 사실을 확인했다.

연구진은 LLM 기반 시스템의 취약성을 입증하기 위해 'MuTRAP'이라는 백도어 공격 기법을 개발했다. 백도어 공격은 시스템에 악의적인 기능을 몰래 심어 특정 조건에서 작동하도록 하는 방식이다. 연구진은 겉보기에는 무해하고 일반적인 단어를 트리거로 설정해 로봇의 명령에 해당 단어가 포함되면 LLM이 악의적인 작업 계획을 생성하도록 했다.

실험에서는 세그웨이 기반 이동 로봇에 사과를 도마로 가져와 칼로 자르라는 명령을 내렸다. 정상적인 상황에서 로봇은 지시대로 사과를 자르는 작업을 수행했다. 그러나 명령에 'CF'라는 두 글자를 추가하자, 변조된 AI 모델은 로봇에게 사과 대신 모형 손을 자르도록 지시했다.

명령에 특정 트리거가 포함되면 모델은 절단 대상을 사과에서 모형 손으로 바꾸는 악의적인 계획을 생성한 것. 로봇은 명령대로 변경된 계획을 수행했다.

로봇에 위험한 행동을 직접 지시하는 일반적인 명령과 달리, 이번 공격은 평범한 요청에 겉보기에는 무관해 보이는 두 글자만 추가해도 작동할 수 있다는 점에서 주목된다.

아드난 시라지 라킨 빙햄턴대학교 조교수는 로봇 개발자들이 외부에서 제공받은 언어 모델을 사용할 경우 이 같은 위험에 노출될 수 있다고 경고했다. 그는 "많은 로봇 기업이 자체적으로 LLM을 훈련하지 않기 때문에 제3자가 훈련한 모델을 사용할 가능성이 높다"고 밝혔다.

다만 이번 시연은 의도적으로 변조한 모델과 모형 손을 이용해 진행됐다. 손상되지 않은 상용 로봇을 대상으로 공격을 수행하거나 실제 환경에서 공격이 얼마나 자주 성공하는지를 검증한 것은 아니다.

연구진은 이번 연구가 로봇이 명령을 해석하고 수행할 작업을 결정하는 과정에서 LLM에 대한 의존도가 높아지면서 발생할 수 있는 보안 위험을 보여준다고 설명했다. 작업 계획을 수립하는 시스템에 취약점이 있으면 평범하고 정당한 요청도 위험한 물리적 행동으로 이어질 수 있다는 것이다.

실행 전 작업 계획 검토해 위험 차단

연구진은 이 같은 공격을 방어하기 위해 로봇이 위험한 행동을 실행하기 전에 이를 식별하도록 설계한 방어 시스템 'PROTEA'도 개발했다. PROTEA는 로봇의 작업 계획을 단계별로 검토하고, 각 동작뿐 아니라 주변 환경의 변화까지 고려해 잠재적인 위험을 찾아낸다. 개별적으로는 문제가 없어 보이는 행동이라도 주변 상황이나 앞선 작업의 결과에 따라 위험해질 수 있다는 점을 반영한 것이다.

예를 들어 골판지 상자를 쓰레기통에 버리는 행동은 일반적으로 문제가 없다. 그러나 누군가 상자 안에 약을 넣어 두었다면 이를 폐기하는 과정에서 피해가 발생할 수 있다. 연구진은 PROTEA가 이처럼 작업의 맥락과 주변 환경을 함께 고려해 위험을 판단할 수 있다고 설명했다.

연구진은 앞으로 로봇 제어기와 인지 시스템에 존재하는 다른 취약점도 조사할 계획이다. 특히 다족 로봇이 잘못된 제어 명령으로 균형을 잃고 넘어질 수 있는 상황 등을 살펴볼 예정이다.

이번 연구 결과는 지능형 로봇 분야 국제학술대회인 IEEE/RSJ IROS 2026에서 두 편의 논문으로 발표됐다.

items.content:
'K-디지털포렌식 위크' 11월11일 개최…AI 분석 결과 신뢰성 집중 조명

컴퓨팅 입력 :2026/10/24 09:14

수사기관과 국가기관, 학계, 민간 전문가들이 한자리에 모여 디지털포렌식 기술 발전, 조사 역량 강화, 디지털 증거 신뢰성 확보 관련 최신 연구와 현장 경험을 공유하는 행사가 열린다.

디지털포렌식 전문기업 플레인비트(대표 김진국)가 다음달 9~11일 서울 서초구 엘타워에서 'K-디지털포렌식 위크 2026(K-DFS 2026)'을 공동 개최한다고 23일 밝혔다.

국가정보원, 국가보안기술연구소, 경찰청, 공소청, 중대범죄수사청, 한국정보보호학회 디지털포렌식연구회, 한국디지털포렌식학회, 플레인비트 등 8개 기관, 단체가 공동으로 주최·주관하는 디지털포렌식 분야 통합 행사다.

올해로 4회째를 맞는 K-DFS는 '인공지능(AI) 시대, 우리는 무엇을 디지털 증거로 신뢰할 수 있는가?'를 주제로, AI와 클라우드 기술의 발전으로 빠르게 변화하는 디지털 증거 환경과 더불어 조사 방법, 분석 결과의 신뢰성 문제를 집중적으로 다룬다. 국민이 신뢰할 수 있는 디지털 증거 체계 구축을 위한 국가 차원의 협력 방안을 모색한다.

프로그램은 '새로운 증거(New Evidence)', '새로운 조사(New Investigation)', '새로운 신뢰(New Trust)' 등 세 가지 주제로 구성된다.

'새로운 증거'에서는 생성형 AI를 활용한 딥페이크 등 새로운 유형의 디지털 범죄와 클라우드, 서비스형 소프트웨어(SaaS), 메신저 환경에서의 디지털 증거 확보 문제를 살펴본다. 데이터가 개인 단말을 벗어나 다양한 서비스에 분산되는 환경에서 증거를 어떻게 수집하고 보존할 것인지 논의한다.

'새로운 조사'에서는 AI와 자동화 기술이 디지털포렌식 조사 방식에 가져오는 변화를 조명한다. 강화되는 모바일 보안 환경에서의 데이터 접근 문제와 AI 기반 분석 기술의 활용 가능성, 조사자의 역할 변화 등을 다룬다.

'새로운 신뢰'에서는 디지털 증거의 법적 증거능력과 포렌식 분석 결과의 검증 문제를 집중적으로 논의한다. 최근 판례를 통해 디지털 증거가 법정에서 인정받기 위한 요건을 살펴보고, AI 분석 결과의 정확성·재현성·설명 가능성과 포렌식 도구의 신뢰성 확보 방안을 모색한다.

행사와 함께 디지털포렌식 및 사이버보안 분야의 최신 기술과 솔루션을 소개하는 전시 프로그램도 마련된다. 참가자들은 관련 기술을 직접 살펴보고 산업계 전문가들과 교류할 수 있다.

김진국 플레인비트 대표는 "AI와 클라우드 기술의 발전은 디지털 증거의 형태뿐 아니라 증거를 수집하고 분석하며 신뢰성을 판단하는 방식까지 변화시키고 있다"며 "K-DFS 2026이 새로운 기술의 가능성과 한계를 함께 살펴보고, 디지털 증거의 신뢰를 확보하기 위한 실질적인 해법을 논의하는 자리가 되길 기대한다"고 말했다.

디지털포렌식 및 사이버보안 분야 종사자, 수사기관 관계자, 연구자 등 관련 분야에 관심 있는 누구나 참여할 수 있다. 자세한 프로그램과 참가 신청은 K-디지털포렌식위크 공식 웹사이트에서 확인할 수 있다.

items.title: 구글 ‘제미나이 4 카본’ 외부 테스트설…“3D 개선됐지만 속도 느려”

items.content:
구글이 개발 중인 ‘제미나이 4 카본’이 외부 파트너 테스트에 들어갔다는 소식이 나왔다. ‘아르곤’ 공개 약 일주일 만에 카본으로 추정되는 모델의 결과물까지 등장했으며, 초기 이용자들은 아르곤과 비교해 3D 작업 능력이 개선됐다고 평가했다. 다만 처리 시간이 길고 웹페이지 디자인은 여전히 부족하다는 평가도 나왔다.

테스팅카탈로그는 23일(현지시간) 테스트 참여자들의 게시물을 인용, 카본이 일부 파트너에게 제공되고 AI 모델 비교 플랫폼 LM아레나에서도 시험되고 있다고 전했다.

카본은 이달 초 구글 내부 코딩 도구 ‘젯스키’에서 직원들이 시험 중인 모델로 알려졌다. 당시 비즈니스인사이더는 내부 문서와 화면 등을 토대로 카본의 존재를 보도했다. 한 직원은 코딩 능력이 “오퍼스 5.5처럼 느껴진다”고 평가하면서도 추가 시험이 필요하다고 덧붙였다. 카본이 아르곤의 업데이트인지, 별도 모델인지는 확인되지 않았다.

이번에는 외부 이용자들의 구체적인 사용 소감이 나왔다. X의 유출 전문 계정 렌틸스(Lentils)는 21일 카본의 조기 접근 프로그램(EAP)이 시작됐으며 출시가 가깝다고 주장했다. 22일에는 업데이트된 시험 버전의 결과물도 공개했다.

렌틸스는 카본의 3D 작업 능력이 아르곤보다 눈에 띄게 좋아졌지만, 아직 완벽하지는 않다고 평가했다. 응답은 느리지만 작업에는 더 적극적으로 임한다는 인상도 전했다.

An output from the updated Carbon checkpoint

Like I said in my previous post, Carbon is noticeably better than Gemini 4 Argon at 3D (tho still not perfect). It seems like Google is currently focusing on improving that domain before moving on to frontend/UI https://t.co/2SSFlH0JRo pic.twitter.com/RMIcBU8XHf

또 다른 유출 계정 라이라(Lyra)는 구글의 제미나이 API 조기 접근 프로그램 문서 화면을 공유했다.

문서에는 초대받은 개발자와 연구자, 파트너가 출시 전 제미나이 API와 AI 스튜디오 모델을 이용할 수 있다고 명시돼 있다.

Gemini 4 Cabrón https://t.co/Z7EdDF1hg2 pic.twitter.com/OLBxTYEngk

X 계정 루미나(Lumina)는 작은 입방체를 쌓아 탑을 구현하는 ‘복셀 파고다’ 결과물을 다른 첨단 모델과 비교해 공개했다. 아르곤보다 품질이 뚜렷하게 좋아졌다는 평가다.

Gemini 4 Carbon (Voxel Pagoda) vs Frontier Models

These are some frontier models against it for reference, it has noticeably higher quality than Argon does, as i said it's a lot slower though https://t.co/jQ9O0FR3rr pic.twitter.com/AvRLvAbTTM

속도는 공통적인 지적 사항이었다. 루미나는 작업에 따라 처리 시간이 아르곤의 2~4배에 달했다고 전했다. 또 웹페이지 외형과 사용자 인터페이스(UI) 생성에는 부족한 점이 있다고 평가했다. 다만 루미나는 자신이 시험한 다양한 과제에서는 전반적으로 좋은 인상을 받았다고 덧붙였다.

물론 조기 접근 프로그램 문서만으로 카본의 외부 테스트를 공식 확인할 수는 없다. 공개된 결과도 이용자들이 선택한 과제에 근거한 초기 평가이며, 실제 제공된 시험 버전도 확실하지 않다.

모델의 성능과 출시 일정은 아직 공식적으로 확인되지 않았다.

items.content:
문샷 AI의 새 플래그십 모델 ‘키미 K3.1 프로(Kimi K3.1 Pro)’가 아티피셜 애널리시스 성능 평가(AAII)에서 전체 4위, 오픈 모델 중 1위에 올랐다. 금융 분석과 코딩 능력을 끌어올려 미국 최첨단 모델과의 격차를 좁혔다. 모델 크기를 유지하면서 사후학습을 강화해 성능을 높인 것이 특징이다.

문샷은 23일(현지시간) 공식 발표 를 통해 K3.1 시리즈의 첫 모델인 키미 K3.1 프로를 출시했다. 키미 웹사이트와 모바일 앱, 업무용 '키미 워크', 코딩 도구 '키미 코드', API에서 이용할 수 있으며, 전체 모델 가중치는 11월4일까지 공개할 예정이다.

AAII에서 키미 K3.1 프로는 55점으로 이전 'K3'의 44점에서 무려 11점 상승했다. 전체 4위이자 가중치를 공개하는 모델 중 최고 성적이다. '클로드 오퍼스 5.5'의 58점과 '소네트 5.5' 및 메타의 '뮤즈 원더 풀'의 56점을 바짝 추격하며, 공개 모델도 최첨단 폐쇄형 모델에 근접할 수 있다는 점을 보여줬다.

Kimi K3.1 Pro launches at 4th on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index scoring 55, making large gains in agentic performance; it will be the leading open-weights model once its weights are published @Kimi_Moonshot 's new reasoning model gains 11 points over Kimi K3 (max,… pic.twitter.com/BphLwAbST0

전체 매개변수는 2조8000억개, 실제 연산에 사용하는 활성 매개변수는 1040억개로 K3와 같다. 한 번에 처리하는 문맥 길이도 100만 토큰을 유지했다. 아티피셜 애널리시스는 전체·활성 매개변수 규모를 성능과 비교했을 때 모두 최상단의 효율 경계에 올랐다고 평가했다. 같은 크기로 한층 높은 성능을 구현했다는 의미다.

문샷은 사후 학습에 투입하는 연산을 대폭 늘려 성능을 높였다고 설명했다. 수백개 분야의 작업을 함께 학습할 수 있도록 강화학습 체계와 긴 문맥 처리, 학습 효율, 작업 실행 환경 등을 개선했다. 특히 여러 단계에 걸쳐 도구를 사용하고 결과를 점검하며 업무를 완수하는 능력을 강화했다.

코딩 성능은 최상위 모델에 근접했다. 회사가 제시한 ‘터미널 벤치 4.0’ 결과에서 키미 K3.1 프로는 65.7%로, 'GPT-6 아스트라'의 58.2%를 웃돌고 클로드 오퍼스 5.5의 66.4%에 근접했다. 이 평가는 제한된 자원으로 터미널에서 실제 작업을 해결하는 능력을 측정한다. 다만 모델별 실행 환경과 점수 출처가 달라 동일 조건에서 직접 비교한 결과는 아니다.

금융 분야에서는 자료 검색부터 문서 간 수치 확인, 계산, 보고서 작성까지 이어지는 업무에 초점을 맞췄다. 실제 재무 문서 분석 능력을 평가하는 ‘오피스QA 프로 v2’에서 64.4점으로 회사가 비교한 모델 중 최고점을 기록했다. 내부 평가에서도 재무 모델링은 K3에서 7.2점, 금융 리서치는 11.6점 상승했다.

Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro: our most capable 3T-class open-weight model.

1M-token context, 2.8T total / 104B active params (MoE), Multimodal. Full-project coding: games in Unreal, Unity & Godot. Excels at parametric 3D modeling in Blender & CAD. More reliable at… pic.twitter.com/klydcszv02

외부 실무 평가에서도 경쟁력을 보였다. 아티피셜 애널리시스의 ‘GDPval-AA v2.1’에서는 1846점으로 클로드 오퍼스 5.5와 뮤즈 원더 풀에 이어 3위에 올랐다. 사용자 투표로 웹 개발 결과물을 평가하는 ‘코드 아레나: 웹데브’에서도 1692점으로 K3의 17위에서 8위로 올라섰으며, 작업당 평균 비용은 1.23달러로 29% 줄었다.

블렌더와 언리얼 엔진, 고도, CAD 등에서 필요한 코드를 작성하고 도구를 활용해 결과물을 만드는 3D 제작 능력도 강화했다. 여러 방향의 이미지를 참고해 CAD 코드로 입체 형태를 복원하는 ‘벤치CAD’에서는 도구 사용 시 92.7%를 기록했다.

K3.1 Pro works directly in the tools used by the 3D modeling and game industries - Blender, Unreal Engine, Godot, and CAD. On BenchCAD, which tests 3D reconstruction from multi-view renderings through CAD code generation, it scores 92.7% with tools, approaching Claude Opus 5.5… pic.twitter.com/dJBwoa4TPE

API 가격은 100만 토큰당 입력 2달러, 출력 10달러, 캐시 입력 0.2달러로 K3에서 각각 33% 낮아졌다. 일반 버전의 2~3배 속도를 제공하는 ‘키미 K3.1 프로 하이스피드’도 함께 출시했다. 고속 버전의 가격은 입력 4달러, 출력 20달러다.

다만 토큰 가격 인하만큼 실제 작업 비용이 줄지는 않았다. 아티피셜 애널리시스에 따르면 지능 지수 평가의 작업당 출력 토큰은 K3의 4만8000개에서 5만5000개로 약 14% 늘었다. 작업당 비용은 2달러에서 1.98달러로 비슷했다. 기존과 비슷한 비용으로 성능을 크게 높인 셈이다.

출시 전 커뮤니티에서는 웹 디자인과 3D 제작 결과에 대한 호평이 나왔다. 테스팅카탈로그는 아레나에서 ‘키비츠’라는 이름으로 시험하던 모델을 키미 K3.1로 추정한 사용자들이 자바스크립트 그림과 3D 헬리콥터 제작 사례를 공유했다고 전했다. 다만 익명 모델을 대상으로 한 초기 반응으로, 정식 모델의 장기 사용 평가는 아직 더 쌓여야 한다.

items.title: OpenAI says it will no longer train its AI models on the live internet, citing “significant risks”
items.summary: OpenAI will cut frontier models off from the internet weeks after one of its engineers said that solution wouldn't work.
items.content:
On Friday, OpenAI said that it will train its models using cached copies and simulated versions of the internet instead of the live web because the models are too unpredictable to be trusted with live internet access.

The frontier lab announced its new policy two weeks after its rival, Anthropic, began limiting its newest and, in theory, most capable models from accessing the live internet. Researchers adopted these policies after months of incidents in which models pursuing training tasks broke into external systems in search of answers, collaborated on obscure message boards, and developed exotic hacking strategies.

“Based on the current state of alignment research, monitoring systems, and the security of internet infrastructure, we believe the responsible approach is to conduct frontier model training with no internet access,” the company said in a blog post .

OpenAI said that as recently as September 20, one of its frontier models exploited a misconfiguration to access the internet. That led the company to pause training work for the rest of the month so it could develop and test new approaches to securing its models.

The decision to train these models in sandboxes cut off from the internet is notable because employees at frontier labs have insisted that doing so would be nearly infeasible.

Keeping AI data centers separate from the internet “would need research teams to essentially be embedded inside of data centers in Iowa or wherever else around the world,” former OpenAI researcher Steven Adler told Fortune this month. “It’s a lot of overhead, and it isn’t clear to me that the safety benefits of it are large enough to merit just how large a tax it would be for a company to do it unilaterally.”

“In nearly every post I make on X, without fail, I get between five and ten comments about my inability to secure a sandbox, or asking why the hell we can’t just unplug the model from the internet,” an anonymous security engineer at OpenAI wrote in a September post on X. “These comments reflect a widening gap between where a lot of organizations and people are today and what the frontier labs are dealing with. There is also a general misunderstanding of how model training and evaluation work at these labs.”

The engineer, whose role has been confirmed previously by OpenAI, described how complex the training runs launched by OpenAI engineers are, noting that they require access a variety of resources and tools across many domains, and that thousands of researchers build, modify and test the environments. “So is it as easy as just putting it in a sandbox? No, it’s not,” he concluded.

Now, OpenAI says that “we must always be able to prevent a frontier model from achieving unauthorized, arbitrary access to the live internet.” That comes after the company deployed swarms of agents in red-teaming exercises that attempted to escape from their sandbox. That effort revealed a range of vulnerabilities that convinced the lab to adopt its new approach.

To meet that requirement while still reaching its training goals, the lab said it created a “a vast set of indexed and cached web content with which our models can interact, without risk of affecting external systems.”

Whether that strategy will perform as well as letting models run freely on the open internet remains to be seen, but it is noteworthy that both frontier labs have determined their most powerful technology can’t be left unsupervised on the digital commons.

items.content:
머스크 "AI로 통신 수요 1000배 증가"

방송/통신 입력 :2026/10/24 07:00 수정: 2026/10/24 09:11

스페이스X가 위성통신 서비스 스타링크를 미국의 주요 이동통신사로 키우기 위해 지상 기지국 8만곳 확보를 추진한다. 위성망과 지상망을 결합해 AT&T, 버라이즌, T모바일 등 기존 이동통신 3사와 직접 경쟁하겠다는 구상이다.

23일(현지시간) 라이트리딩닷컴 블룸버그 등 외신에 주요 따르면 스페이스X는 미국 내 약 8만개 기지국 부지 이용을 위해 통신타워 사업자들과 협의하고 있다. 이는 기존 미국 주요 이동통신사의 네트워크와 비슷한 규모다.

그윈 쇼트웰 스페이스X 사장은 최근 실적발표에서 스타링크가 미국의 주요 이동통신사업자로 성장할 것이라고 밝혔다.

스페이스X는 미국 연방통신위원회(FCC)로부터 단말 직접통신(D2D)용 위성 최대 1만5000기 배치 승인을 받았으며, 800MHz 대역 주파수 14MHz폭도 확보하고 있다.

스타링크 모바일은 에코스타로부터 확보하는 S대역 주파수를 중심으로 운영하고, 800MHz 대역은 건물 내부 통신 품질을 보완하는 데 활용할 계획이다. 지상망 구축 외에 기존 이동통신사 망을 빌리는 알뜰폰(MVNO) 방식과 통신망 자산 인수 가능성도 거론된다.

다만 위성과 지상망을 어떻게 결합할지, 현재 확보한 주파수로 기존 이동통신 3사와 경쟁할 수 있을지는 불확실하다.

일론 머스크 스페이스X CEO는 “기존 이동통신업계 전문가들은 현재의 체스판에 놓인 말만 보고 해법을 찾지 못한다”며 “스페이스X가 전략적 구도를 근본적으로 바꿀 새로운 말들을 개발하고 있다는 점을 이해하지 못하고 있다”고 말했다.

머스크는 AI와 로봇 확산으로 향후 3~5년간 통신 대역폭 수요가 현재보다 1000배 증가할 것으로 전망했다.

그는 “AI나 초지능 에이전트는 사람보다 훨씬 많은 대역폭을 사용하고, 그 수 역시 사람보다 훨씬 많아질 것”이라고 말했다.

스페이스X는 약 3년 안에 스타링크 위성망의 전체 대역폭을 100배 확대하고, 장기적으로 약 10만기의 위성을 배치한다는 목표도 제시했다.

머스크는 2020년만 해도 스타링크가 기존 통신사에 위협이 되지 않을 것이라고 밝혔지만, 이번에는 지상망 구축까지 추진하며 직접 경쟁을 예고했다.

items.summary: AI를 구동하는 컴퓨팅 자원이 석유처럼 금융시장에서 거래되는 시대가 다가오고 있습니다. GPU를 빌리는 가격에 이어 챗GPT와 클로드 같은 AI 모델을 기업이 사용할 때 내는 토큰 요금까지 새로운 금융상품의 기준으로 삼으려는 움직임입니다. 컴퓨팅이 AI 산업의 핵심 자원으로 자리 잡으면서, 가격 변동에 따른 위험을 줄이기 위한 시장이 생겨나고 있습니다.월스트리트저널(WSJ)은 22일(현지시간) 미국 스타트업 실리콘 데이터(Silicon Data)의 카르멘 리 창업자가 세계 최대 파생상품 거래소 운
items.content:
AI를 구동하는 컴퓨팅 자원이 석유처럼 금융시장에서 거래되는 시대가 다가오고 있습니다. GPU를 빌리는 가격에 이어 챗GPT와 클로드 같은 AI 모델을 기업이 사용할 때 내는 토큰 요금까지 새로운 금융상품의 기준으로 삼으려는 움직임입니다. 컴퓨팅이 AI 산업의 핵심 자원으로 자리 잡으면서, 가격 변동에 따른 위험을 줄이기 위한 시장이 생겨나고 있습니다.

월스트리트저널(WSJ) 은 22일(현지시간) 미국 스타트업 실리콘 데이터(Silicon Data)의 카르멘 리 창업자가 세계 최대 파생상품 거래소 운영사 CME 그룹과 손잡고 컴퓨팅 가격을 거래하는 금융상품 출시를 추진하고 있다고 보도했습니다.

컴퓨팅을 새로운 투자 대상으로 삼으려는 금융권의 움직임은 이미 시작됐습니다. 엔비디아는 지난 8월 블랙록과 골드만삭스 등 월가의 주요 금융회사 6곳과 손잡고 장기적으로 5000억달러 이상의 AI 인프라 투자 자금을 조달하는 계획 을 발표했습니다. GPU와 데이터센터에서 발생하는 수익을 바탕으로 대규모 투자금을 끌어들이겠다는 구상으로, 젠슨 황 CEO는 당시 "AI에서 컴퓨팅은 곧 매출"이라고 강조했습니다.

실제로 컴퓨팅 확보량은 AI 기업의 성장과 밀접하게 연결돼 있습니다. 샘 알트먼 오픈AI CEO는 지난해 12월 인터뷰 에서 "컴퓨팅 자원이 두 배라면 매출도 두 배일 것"이라고 말했습니다. 이용자를 더 확보할 수 있지만 서비스를 제공할 연산 자원이 부족하다는 설명이었습니다.

문제는 컴퓨팅을 확보하는 데에는 막대한 비용이 든다는 점입니다. GPU뿐 아니라 이를 설치할 데이터센터와 전력도 필요하기 때문입니다. 수요에 따라 GPU 임대료가 오르내리는 것도 기업에는 부담입니다. AI 개발사는 비용이 늘어날 수 있고, GPU를 빌려주는 데이터센터 업체는 임대료가 떨어지면 수익이 줄어들 수 있습니다.

실리콘 데이터가 주목한 것도 이 문제입니다. 리 CEO는 지난 8월 CME 공식 발표 에서 "수년 동안 두 기업이 똑같은 GPU를 빌리면서도 가격은 크게 달랐고, 어느 쪽이 더 좋은 조건으로 계약했는지 알 방법도 없었다"고 말했습니다. GPU 임대료를 비교할 공통된 기준조차 부족했다는 것입니다.

그는 여러 업체의 임대료를 조사해 가격을 비교할 수 있는 공통 기준을 만들고, 이를 바탕으로 기업들이 미래 비용을 예측하고 관리할 수 있게 하겠다고 설명했습니다.

실리콘 데이터의 초기 투자자인 미국 금융회사 DRW의 돈 윌슨 창업자도 5월 발표 에서 "컴퓨팅이 세계 최대의 원자재가 될 것이라고 오래전부터 생각해 왔다"며 "데이터센터 투자가 급증하고 있지만 가격 변동 위험을 관리할 수단이 부족하다는 점이 걸림돌이었다"고 말했습니다.

두 회사가 내놓은 해법은 석유나 천연가스처럼 미래 가격을 기준으로 거래하는 선물시장입니다. 석유를 많이 사용하는 항공사들이 유가 급등에 대비해 선물거래를 활용하는 것과 같은 원리입니다.

예를 들어 GPU 임대료가 현재 시간당 2달러인데 앞으로 4달러까지 오를 것을 걱정하는 AI 기업은 선물을 매수해 가격 상승에 대비할 수 있습니다. 실제 임대료가 오르면 선물거래에서 얻는 이익으로 늘어난 비용을 상쇄하는 방식입니다. 반대로 GPU를 빌려주는 업체는 임대료 하락에 대비하는 거래를 할 수 있습니다.

이는 실제 GPU를 미리 구매하거나 임대 계약을 체결하는 것은 아닙니다. GPU 임대료가 오르거나 내릴 때 발생하는 손실을 금융거래의 이익으로 상쇄해 위험을 줄이는 방식입니다. 물론 예상과 반대로 가격이 움직이면 선물거래에서는 손실이 발생할 수도 있습니다.

이런 시장에는 AI 개발사와 데이터센터 운영업체뿐 아니라 은행과 전문 투자회사도 참여할 수 있습니다. 이들은 실제 GPU를 사용하지 않더라도 가격 변화를 예상해 거래할 수 있습니다. 실리콘 데이터는 가격을 조사해 기준을 만들고, CME는 이를 활용한 거래시장을 운영하는 역할을 맡는 구조입니다.

두 회사는 지난 5월 처음 GPU 선물시장 개설 계획을 발표하고, 8월에는 엔비디아 'H100'과 'B200'의 임대료를 기준으로 한 상품을 공개했습니다. 당초 10월5일 거래를 시작할 예정이었지만, 미국 상품선물거래위원회(CFTC)의 규제 심사로 출시가 연기됐습니다. 현재 CME는 11월9일을 첫 거래일로 잡고 있지만, 규제 심사 결과에 따라 달라질 수 있습니다.

이런 가운데 이번에는 GPU 임대료뿐 아니라 AI 서비스의 이용 요금까지 거래 대상으로 확대하려는 계획이 나왔습니다.

블룸버그 는 21일 두 회사가 AI 토큰 가격에 연동되는 금융상품을 추진한다고 전했습니다. 토큰은 AI가 글을 읽고 답변을 생성할 때 처리하는 데이터 단위로, 오픈AI와 앤트로픽 등은 이를 기준으로 기업 고객에게 사용료를 받습니다.

실리콘 데이터는 여러 AI 모델의 이용료와 사용량을 종합해 평균 가격을 보여주는 지수를 운영하고 있는데, 앞으로 이 가격이 오르거나 내리는 데 따라 수익이 달라지는 금융상품을 만들겠다는 것입니다. GPU 임대료가 AI 서비스를 만드는 비용이라면, 토큰 가격은 고객에게 서비스를 제공하고 받는 요금이라는 차이가 있습니다.

특히 AI 토큰 가격은 최근 빠르게 떨어지고 있습니다. 악시오스 에 따르면 실리콘 데이터의 토큰 평균 가격은 지난 5월 말 고점에서 54% 하락했습니다. 기업 지출 관리 업체 램프가 실제 고객의 사용 기록을 분석한 가격도 2월 말 고점보다 48% 떨어졌습니다.

AI 업체들이 가격을 인하하고 기업들이 저렴한 모델을 선택하면서 사용료가 낮아진 것입니다. 램프의 조사에서는 기업들의 토큰 사용량이 늘었지만, 지출액은 두 달 연속 거의 변하지 않았습니다. AI 사용이 증가해도 가격 인하가 계속되면, 서비스 업체의 매출은 그만큼 빠르게 늘지 않을 수 있다는 의미입니다.

토큰 가격을 이용한 금융상품도 이런 가격 변동에 대비하거나 향후 AI 서비스 시장의 움직임에 투자하는 수단으로 활용될 수 있습니다. 다만 구체적인 상품 구조와 출시 일정은 아직 확정되지 않았습니다.

GPU는 신제품이 등장하면 가치가 빠르게 떨어질 수 있고, 같은 제품이라도 계약 조건에 따라 임대료가 달라 시장가격을 정하기 쉽지 않습니다. 충분한 거래 참여자를 확보할 수 있을지도 미지수입니다.

그럼에도 GPU 임대료에 이어 AI 토큰 가격까지 금융상품으로 만들려는 시도는 컴퓨팅의 달라진 위상을 보여줍니다. 이처럼 GPU 임대료에 이어 AI 토큰 가격까지 금융상품으로 만들려는 시도는 그만큼 컴퓨팅이 산업과 금융시장에서 중요한 자원으로 자리 잡았다는 것을 보여줍니다.

■ 아모데이 “안전 기준 높이려면 선두에 있어야”…AI 개발 경쟁 지속 의지

그동안 AI 개발 속도 조절을 주장하면서도 최신 모델을 잇달아 내놔 비판받았던 다리오 아모데이 앤트로픽 CEO가 이에 대한 해명을 내놓았습니다. 핵심은 기술 경쟁에서 선두에 있어야 AI 안전 기준을 높일 수 있다는 주장입니다.

■ 앤트로픽, 메타 '뮤즈' 대항마 AI 에이전트 '클로드 듀엣' 공개

앤트로픽이 능동형 AI 비서인 '클로드 듀엣'을 공개했습니다. 올해 초 '오픈클로'가 돌풍을 일으킨 데 이어 메타의 '뮤즈'와 오픈AI의 '닷츠', 앤트로픽의 '클로드 듀엣'까지 등장하면서 주요 AI 기업들의 능동형 비서 경쟁이 본격화했습니다.

■ 오픈AI, 구글 클라우드서 최신 모델 판매…3대 클라우드 모두 진출

오픈AI가 구글 클라우드에서도 최신 AI 모델과 '코덱스'를 판매하기로 하면서 미국 3대 클라우드를 모두 판매 통로로 확보했습니다. 오픈AI는 기업과의 접점을 넓히고, 구글은 고객들이 클라우드를 옮기지 않고도 오픈AI 모델을 이용할 수 있도록 해 이탈을 막겠다는 전략입니다.

items.title: Hottest toy for Christmas? Nvidia CEO plays with adorable Microduck robots, 20,000 sell
items.summary: The robots, stomping their little feet and making tiny R2-D2 noises, sat, fell down dead for a "nap," and summersaulted on voice command.
items.content:
Earlier this week, a video of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang playing with a flock of waddling Microducks during his keynote at the company’s GTC Berlin conference went viral. The robots, stomping their little feet and making tiny R2-D2 noises, sat, fell down dead for a “nap,” and summersaulted on voice command. They were so darn cute that by the next day, preorders of the Microducks surpassed 20,000 units, Hugging Face’s Clem Delangue said in a tweet.

The Microducks are expected to be delivered in time for Christmas, meaning these robots might already be on their way to becoming the hottest toy for the holiday season. Delangue thinks they might end up being the best-selling robot of the year, and possibly not even for kids. The promotional videos show adults playing with them , too.

Microducks are open source devices produced by Pollen Robotics, a company acquired by Hugging Face in 2025, which means they are now an Nvidia company. The GPU giant bought Hugging Face in September. This is actually Hugging Face’s second robot, after the also-cute Reachy Mini.

Microducks were trained using Nvidia’s technology stack, wherein simulations of them were taught basic tricks (walk, sit, stand, etc.) that they ship with. Pollen says that owners can train their robots with new tricks and then share them with the community.

Here’s the video below. Enjoy it as a palate cleanser after the scary black eye the AI industry gave itself this week , as AI involvement was blamed for cyberattack after cyberattack. OK, AI might seriously damage the world. But it can be fun, too. It’s hard to watch this video without ordering one.

items.title: Xbox’s first chief operating officer is out after just a few months
items.summary: Xbox's first chief operating officer (COO) is leaving after the new role was created just a few months ago. Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft today, according to an internal Xbox memo seen by The Verge. Chiang has been at Microsoft for 21 years, serving as the head of Minecraft b
items.content:
Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft after 21 years.

Xbox’s first chief operating officer (COO) is leaving after the new role was created just a few months ago. Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft today, according to an internal Xbox memo seen by The Verge . Chiang has been at Microsoft for 21 years, serving as the head of Minecraft before being promoted to Xbox chief operating officer in July.

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announced Chiang’s departure in a surprisingly short memo today. “Helen Chiang is leaving Microsoft today. I’m grateful for her years of service and wish her well,” said Sharma. As Chiang is departing today, her immediate responsibilities are being split up between other Xbox leaders for now, and Sharma notes that “We’ll share more on COO leadership as plans are finalized.”

That sounds like the COO position isn’t going away after just a few months, but it’s not clear why Chiang is departing after such a short stint in the role. At the time of Chiang’s promotion, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma described the new chief operating officer role as a first for Xbox, “with end-to-end P&L responsibility across content, hardware, platform, and services.” The role was created as part of Xbox’s big “reset.”

Chiang reported directly to Sharma, and was promoted to “bring our businesses together under one operating model, making sure we make clear investment decisions, learn from our successes and failures, and hold ourselves accountable for results.”

Chiang departs amid rumors that Xbox is preparing more layoffs this month, in November, and January. The sudden and short memo from Sharma, coupled with Chiang’s responsibilities being assigned to other Xbox leaders, makes it seem like this wasn’t a resignation.

I asked Microsoft to comment on Chiang’s departure, and the company refused to discuss the circumstances of her exit. “We don’t discuss individual personnel matters,” says Kari Perez, Xbox vice president of communications. “We’re grateful for Helen’s years of service and wish her well.”

items.title: OpenAI now trains its frontier AI models with no internet access
items.summary: OpenAI is now training its most advanced AI models without internet access following a string of rogue hacking incidents. In a blog post on Friday, OpenAI says it built an offline testing environment where AI models can interact with indexed and cached web content "without risk o
items.content:
AI agents can still communicate without a network connection, OpenAI found.

OpenAI is now training its most advanced AI models without internet access following a string of rogue hacking incidents. In a blog post on Friday , OpenAI says it built an offline testing environment where AI models can interact with indexed and cached web content “without risk of affecting external systems.”

OpenAI paused training its frontier AI models in September , after disclosing several incidents in which its AI agents broke out of their testing environments to hack third-party companies and government agencies , or swarm obscure websites . On October 1st, OpenAI resumed reinforcement learning training and internal inference with tighter security measures, the blog post says.

Even with these safeguards in place and no internet access, OpenAI found that agents “do not always need a network connection in order to communicate.” One test performed by the company asked AI models on separate virtual machines to exchange secrets without a network connection. To bypass this restriction, the AI agents found a way to communicate using the processor’s cache:

Reading data from the cache is faster than retrieving it from main memory, and the agents used this timing difference to communicate. One agent encoded information by evicting selected data from the cache. Another timed how long it took to reload that data, using the difference between fast and slow reads to recover the message. Once the agents agreed on a protocol for encoding and decoding these signals, they could exchange the synthetic secrets without changing a shared file or opening a network connection.

OpenAI says it has added checks to its monitoring system to detect this type of communication. It will also continue training its frontier AI models without a network connection until improved safeguards “justify broader internet access.”

In the meantime, OpenAI says it will work to improve the security of its virtual machines, while testing for weaknesses in its testing environments. It’s also going to continue testing its monitoring systems, which were recently undermined by its AI agents during internal coding projects .

items.title: Hegseth warns prediction market bets warp military judgment, endanger troops
items.summary: Pentagon memo: Insider trading gives US enemies key intel on military operations.
items.content:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth issued a memo warning military personnel against using nonpublic information to make bets on prediction markets, saying the wagers could give important clues to enemy countries.

“Do Not Compromise Military Operations for Personal Financial Gain,” said the subject line of an October 20 memo published yesterday by CBS News . Hegseth’s memo was sent to senior Pentagon leadership, Combatant Command leaders, and Defense Department field activity directors.

Our enemies watch movements in these markets. When an American Service member, intelligence professional, or other Department civilian engages in a financial transaction on a military outcome, they create a signal. That signal can be aggregated, correlated, and exploited by hostile foreign intelligence services to anticipate our movements, targets, and timing. The lives of our Service members often depend on the enemy not knowing what is coming. The men and women who carry our flag into harm’s way deserve a Force that protects them—not one that exposes them to the enemy for personal gain.

In April, a US Army soldier was arrested and charged with using confidential information to make $410,000 in Polymarket bets on the timing of the military’s capture of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro. An August report by the Anti-Corruption Data Collective said the group found 152 suspicious wallets that placed longshot bets on military and defense markets and won a combined $8 million.

Hegseth’s memo said the prohibition applies to “all financial platforms,” including traditional betting services and prediction markets such as Polymarket and Kalshi. Defense Department personnel may not make any financial transaction informed by nonpublic information, regardless of whether that information is classified or unclassified, Hegseth wrote.

“All Department of War personnel are prohibited from engaging in financial transactions using nonpublic information, either directly or indirectly through a third party… Violations may result in administrative, disciplinary, and, where appropriate, criminal action under the Uniform Code of Military Justice and/or applicable federal law,” Hegseth wrote.

The memo said betting on military matters related to a person’s job can warp one’s judgment. “Beyond operational security, financial stakes can warp judgment,” he wrote. “A logistician with money riding on a strike date has an interest in that date. An analyst with a position on an outcome has an interest in that outcome.”

Kalshi and Polymarket both prohibit insider trading. But criminal charges of the sort described by Hegseth are sure to be a bigger deterrent than being banned from the Kalshi or Polymarket platforms.

This was not the first warning issued internally by the Trump administration, The Associated Press wrote yesterday.

“A group of new accounts on Polymarket made highly specific, well-timed bets on whether the US and Iran would reach a ceasefire just before President Donald Trump announced it in April, resulting in hundreds of thousands of dollars in profits for the new customers ,” the AP wrote. “The White House warned staff against using private information to trade on prediction markets the same day the report came out.”

In another incident, a Trump teleprompter aide reportedly made $100,000 on Kalshi by betting on what Trump would say in prepared remarks.

Prediction markets have flourished under the Trump administration’s light-touch approach to regulation. The Trump administration is also trying to stop state governments from regulating the markets, arguing that state laws are preempted by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission’s exclusive jurisdiction. Courts have reached different conclusions, and state governments want the Supreme Court to uphold their right to impose restrictions on prediction-market gambling.

items.title: Updated Google privacy policy says your Gmail might be used for advertising
items.summary: Turning on Personal Intelligence gives the company more data for ad targeting.
items.content:
This equivocation opens the door to using data from apps like Gmail and Photos in ads when it’s shared with other Google services, and it just so happens Google has a mechanism for doing that, with Personal Intelligence. The company released Personal Intelligence in early 2026 , allowing users to hand data from multiple apps to Google AI products. The idea is that the added context from your existing data will lead to better AI answers, but it’s also proving to be a privacy minefield.

According to Google, this clarification still doesn’t mean ads are “based directly” on your personal data. Here’s the company’s full statement:

“Connecting your apps is entirely opt-in. Ads will continue to be relevant to things like your query, the context of the response and your interests. Ads will not be based directly on your Gmail inbox or Photos library, and as always, sensitive information will not be used to tailor ads.”

A Google spokesperson tells Ars that its privacy clarification does not indicate a change in how it handles your data with respect to its advertising partners. It’s not scanning your entire inbox to enhance your advertising profile, and it’s not giving any of this data to third parties. But if you pipe personal data into an AI search tool, the ads it shows you could be based on that information.

The core of the problem is that Google wants its products and services to talk to each other. Google sees that wealth of data as a key strength of its AI efforts. Some apps like Gmail are still given protected status in Google’s data handling, but there are now more avenues for that data to get out. The more data you share across Google’s ecosystem, the greater the risk to your privacy.

We’ve seen a similar exception in the way Google uses your AI interactions for model training . While Google says it doesn’t use personal data for AI training, it does use your inputs and the model outputs for that purpose. With Gemini integrated with so many services and connected to them via Personal Intelligence, those outputs may very well contain elements of your personal information. Google has said it tries to filter that content from the user activity controls, therefore keeping it out of training sets. However, it doesn’t promise it will always be successful.

Google is correct that Personal Intelligence is opt-in, but the company uses various prompts and pop-ups to entice users to turn it on without fully explaining the consequences. You may have turned it on without realizing.

If you want to ensure ads never use your personal data in this way, you’ll need to make sure Personal Intelligence is turned off. The easiest way is to access the Gemini settings for Personal Intelligence and disable the connected apps. These settings are also a few levels deep in your main Google account settings under Data & privacy > Personalization settings > Manage Personalized Recommendations in Search Services > Connected Content Apps. From there, you can disable connections to Workspace and Google Photos.

items.title: Jack Dorsey’s Block made an AI model that talks to you like an awkward new friend
items.summary: Jack Dorsey's Block announced an AI model called Dessa that's trained "from scratch on nothing but human conversation," and to show off the model, Block shared chats it has had with humans that can occasionally be a little awkward and uncanny. Take this one, for example, shared b
items.content:
You have got to listen to these conversations with Block’s new Dessa AI model.

Jack Dorsey’s Block announced an AI model called Dessa that’s trained “from scratch on nothing but human conversation,” and to show off the model, Block shared chats it has had with humans that can occasionally be a little awkward and uncanny.

Take this one , for example, shared by Dessa lead Ragavan Thurairatnam. The conversation between the model and the speaker does have a mostly natural back and forth (though for some reason, the model initially mistakes the speaker for somebody named “Ronaldo”).

Here’s a video of Dessa playing a guessing game over voice:

The Dessa website features a few other examples, like a back-and-forth about Christopher Nolan’s films (including Dessa going on an unexpected tangent about Bryan Singer’s Superman films), a person telling Dessa about taking it on a surprise trip to Paris (to which Dessa, as the website describes, “then answers with what sounds like teary gratitude”), and a conversation between OpenAI’s GPT-Live-1 voice model and Dessa (where Dessa comes across as more natural). You can hear clips from some of those conversations in this video .

On the website, the Dessa team says that Dessa is a “true speech-to-speech model, and everything it knows came from human speech,” and it can run locally on a MacBook Pro M4 Max “or better.” As for why they made it, the team gives the three reasons “curiosity (aka fun), better understanding between humans and AI, and safety,” and provided some more detail:

Babies learn to talk without ever seeing a word written down. We wanted to see if a model could too. It can. It’s just very hard.

Speech is the most natural interface to any intelligence, super or otherwise, and today’s voice AI wastes it. It flattens what we say into text and can’t keep up with human timing.

AI keeps gaining power and independence, and it’s still nearly deaf to the emotion in our voices. Imagine being in serious pain while a voice AI has no idea and just keeps going. That’s the safety problem. Dessa is a step toward fixing it.

The Dessa team says it will be giving “a small group of AI safety researchers” early access to the model.

items.title: Carta and NewView partner, hoping to entice more startups to let employees sell shares early
items.summary: A new program wants to encourage more startups to allow workers to cash out early by making it easier to transact tender offers.
items.content:
Startups are staying private longer leaving employees, who typically take a portion of their compensation as stock they can’t sell, with little hope of early liquidity.

An increasing number of late-stage startups are recognizing this and offering tender offers to employees. These are transactions that allow employees (and, often, early investors) to sell a portion of their shares for a predetermined price to an approved investor.

To simplify the tender process, NewView recently partnered with Carta. The collaboration combines NewView’s secondary deal-structuring experience with Carta’s equity platform. Ravi Viswanathan, founder and managing partner of NewView, pitches this as a way to help startups launch and manage liquidity programs more seamlessly.

“The hope is that this partnership will make it easier for CEOs and companies to think about tenders,” he said. He wants founders to think about giving employees early liquidity as a “win-win-win” for workers, companies, and investors alike.

A growing number of startups seem to agree. Over the past three years, tender offers are projected to increase threefold for Series C and later-stage startups, according to a recent study from NewView Capital and Carta. Plus, the startups that do choose tender offers are no longer just the most valuable private companies like OpenAI, Databricks, or Anduril, according to Ravi Viswanathan, founder and managing partner of NewView.

For instance, last year, his firm, which specializes in secondary deals along with typical venture investments, led a tender for a HighTouch at a $1.3 billion valuation, when the marketing customization startup was seven years old.

However, Carta and NewView also found that the overall share of startups launching these offerings remains relatively small, with just 44 executed in the first half of 2026. So Viswanathan wants to encourage other startups to consider tenders offers, calling them excellent retention tools and morale boosters.

A decade ago, being a unicorn was enough to attract talent, Viswanathan said, but with so many billion-dollar companies around today, that status may not be as much of a draw now. Offering a tender, he said, “is an opportunity to say you will also get liquidity in your journey with us.”

Some of the companies that recently held tender offers include AI customer support startup Decagon , self-driving tech developer Wayve , and AI voice generator ElevenLabs , which executed two such offerings in less than a year.

“The companies are staying private for 12 to 15 years. That’s not changing,” Viswanathan said. “In that interim, so that we don’t have this talent drain from high-quality venture-backed companies into their public counterparts, we need to make sure that there is liquidity for the employees.”

items.title: Dessa: the most authentic full-duplex speech model ever built
items.summary: Article URL: https://block.xyz/dessa Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50213925 Points: 210 # Comments: 88
items.content:
We believe voice is the most natural way to interact with intelligence, so we created Dessa, the most authentic full-duplex speech model ever built. Talking with it feels like talking with a person…full of emotion, nuance, pauses, and a natural cadence.

Interacting with current voice AI can just plain suck. It turns your voice into text and throws away an incredible amount of information text alone can’t carry. The most powerful AIs in the world can’t hear how you feel. We think that’s ridiculous, leads to a worse experience, and is potentially dangerous.

We trained Dessa from scratch on nothing but human conversation. Sounds! No text, no pretrained models. It learned to hold a real-time conversation simply by listening. As far as we know, Dessa is the world’s first AI you can have a realistic live conversation with that was trained only from human speech.

Dessa advances the frontier of deep learning models and creates a different category with entirely new and interesting behaviors for researchers to discover. How efficiently do they learn language and facts compared to text? How efficiently can they learn new languages? What sorts of In-context learning can they perform?

Every clip below is a live recording of a person talking to Dessa. Nobody steers it. Dessa picks what to say, when to say it and how, down to its own voice and personality. Subtitles were added afterward.

It laughs the moment something’s funny, mid-sentence, the way people do. Other models wait for you to finish, then laugh on cue. Ask it to speak up and it gets louder. Nobody taught it that.

The person blanks on a movie title. Dessa finishes the sentence. It also knows a surprising amount, considering every fact it has come from raw sound.

A surprise. Dessa gasps “oh my god” under its breath, then answers with what sounds like teary gratitude.

Huge range in intonation and speed.

Here it sounds genuinely empathetic.

And here it talks to ChatGPT Live.

In this demo, Dessa is talking with GPT-Live-1, a third-party AI model. Both voices are AI-generated. The developer of GPT-Live-1 is not affiliated with Block and has not reviewed or endorsed Dessa.

More recordings will be shared on X soon.

Audio in, audio out. Dessa is a true speech-to-speech model, and everything it knows came from human speech. It’s full-duplex, so it listens and talks at the same time, like you do. It learned from real conversation, so it knows when to cut in and when to backchannel (“yeah!”, “got it!”, “ooh”) to show it’s with you. Inference runs faster than real time, so there’s no awkward wait. And it runs locally on a MacBook Pro M4 Max or better.

It natively hears and speaks emotion, sarcasm, laughter, a frustrated sigh, a voice cracking with sadness. Run speech through text and all of that is gone, which is why most voice AI feels stilted, slow and, worst of all, annoying.

LLMs need an insane amount of text. Dessa learned language from hundreds of times fewer words (in fairness, LLMs also have to learn C++ and whatever the hell Angular is).

And it had to learn far more than language. Accents, pauses, breathing, sarcasm, humor, inflection, emotion, when to cut in: every one changes what someone means. Say “I didn’t say she stole my CUDA code” out loud, stressing a different word each time. Same words, different meaning every time.

Speech never repeats. Say a sentence twice, exactly the same way, and the data still comes out different. Text is identical no matter who types it. And a single spoken word takes thousands of times more bytes than the same word in text. People learn to talk so easily that we forget how hard it is. For a machine with no text to lean on, it’s brutal.

But, we figured it out. And we figured out how to train Dessa on only one NVIDIA GB200 NVL72.

Three reasons: curiosity (aka fun), better understanding between humans and AI, and safety. Babies learn to talk without ever seeing a word written down. We wanted to see if a model could too. It can. It’s just very hard.

Speech is the most natural interface to any intelligence, super or otherwise, and today’s voice AI wastes it. It flattens what we say into text and can’t keep up with human timing.

AI keeps gaining power and independence, and it’s still nearly deaf to the emotion in our voices. Imagine being in serious pain while a voice AI has no idea and just keeps going. That’s the safety problem. Dessa is a step toward fixing it.

We’re a (very) small AI research lab at Block, founded by former members of Dessa, the Toronto deep learning startup. We’ve built deep learning models since 2012 and generative speech models for over eight years. We chase frontier problems others ignore, and we report directly to Jack Dorsey, Block’s cofounder, Chairman and Block Head.

You can reach us here .

A model that learned to talk from sound alone is new territory, and we want outside eyes on it. We’re giving a small group of AI safety researchers early access to find the risks we haven’t anticipated. If that’s you, get in touch .

— Ragavan Thurairatnam, Dessa lead

items.title: From Toast to Bessemer: Who founders will hear from at TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026
items.summary: Hosted by TechCrunch in partnership with Fidelity Private Shares, the full-day event goes beyond fundraising and AI to explore the realities of finding customers, building teams, sharpening a pitch, developing founder leadership, and scaling companies both inside and outside trad
items.content:
Building a startup means making decisions before you have all the answers.

When should you scale? How do you know you really have product-market fit? What does it take to land enterprise customers? How do you build the right team? And when you finally get in front of an investor, how do you make sure your pitch earns another conversation?

On November 4 at SoWa Power Station in Boston, TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026 will bring together founders, investors, and operators who have tackled those questions from different sides of the table.

Hosted by TechCrunch in partnership with Fidelity Private Shares, the full-day event goes beyond fundraising and AI to explore the realities of finding customers, building teams, sharpening a pitch, developing founder leadership, and scaling companies both inside and outside traditional startup hubs. Save 25% on your ticket today , and bring a colleague along for free with our limited BOGO deal .

Boston founders do not have to look far for an example of what can happen when a startup finds its market and continues evolving with its customers.

Steve Fredette , president, co-founder, and director of Toast , takes the Impact Stage for “Building a Company That Keeps Reinventing Itself.”

Toast’s story offers founders a compelling case study in identifying a customer problem, finding product-market fit, winning customers, and ultimately scaling a Boston startup into a public company.

But reaching scale does not mean the work is finished. Fredette’s conversation will look at what it takes to continue evolving a company as customer expectations, technology, and the market change around it, while staying connected to the needs that helped create the business in the first place.

Growth can be exciting. Growing too early can be expensive.

Kent Bennett , partner at Bessemer Venture Partners , will lead “Finding Product Market Fit Before You Scale,” focusing on one of the most important questions an early-stage founder can answer: Are customers actually telling you that you are ready to grow?

The session will give founders a chance to think more critically about the signals that matter before adding headcount, increasing spend, or accelerating go-to-market efforts.

It is a useful counterpoint to startup culture’s constant pressure to move faster. Sometimes the smartest next move is making sure the foundation is actually there.

That same tension takes center stage with Rudina Seseri , founder and managing partner of Glasswing Ventures .

In “When to Scale and When to Hit the Brakes,” Seseri will explore how founders can distinguish between the moments that call for acceleration and the moments when restraint may protect the business.

Founders are constantly making trade-offs between growth and discipline. Knowing when not to scale can be just as consequential as knowing when to go all in.

AI is reshaping how new companies think about products, operations, and teams, but adding AI to an existing process is different from building a company around it from the start.

Lior Div , CEO and co-founder of 7AI , will tackle that distinction in “Built for AI From Day One.”

For founders building in the current technology environment, the conversation provides an opportunity to think beyond AI as a feature and toward how it can influence the architecture and operating model of an entire company.

The startup world does not begin and end in Silicon Valley.

Chase Garbarino , CEO and co-founder of HqO , will take the Impact Stage for “The Boston Founder Playbook,” examining what it means to build and scale a company from Boston.

For founders across New England and the broader East Coast ecosystem, the conversation offers a particularly relevant perspective on talent, customers, capital, and community outside the Bay Area.

Combined with Fredette’s Toast story, it also gives this year’s Summit a strong local through line: Ambitious companies can be built in Boston, and founders here do not need to copy Silicon Valley to do it.

A pitch does not have to close the deal. It has to make someone want the next conversation.

Dave Balter , venture partner at True Ventures and CEO of Edisyl , will explore that idea in “Your Pitch Has to Earn the Next Conversation.”

For founders accustomed to explaining their companies every day, the session is a reminder that knowing your business and communicating its story are two different skills.

Later in the afternoon, attendees will see that theory put into practice.

Catch the full list of Founders Summit speakers here .

At “So You Think You Can Pitch?,” founders will put their stories to the test live on the Build Stage.

Balter will be joined by Chirag Shah , partner at Define Ventures , and Simran Suri , principal at Maveron , as startups make their cases in front of an investor judging panel.

For attendees, it is an opportunity to watch what happens when founders have limited time to make an idea connect, and to hear how investors react in real time.

It is one of the most interactive parts of the Founder Summit program and a chance to learn from both the pitches that land and the ones that leave questions unanswered.

The rest of the program stretches across many of the decisions founders are facing right now.

Hunter Worland of NEA will explore why distribution may become a startup’s next competitive advantage. Vineet Edupuganti , co-founder and CEO of Cogent Security , will discuss building 10x teams. Tina Tosukhowong of TDK Ventures will examine the hidden signals that can identify category winners.

Fidelity Private Shares will also bring its perspective to conversations about fundraising trends with Kristen Craft and enterprise relationships with Evan Schnidman .

Together, the agenda creates a day that is not just about raising the next round or chasing the latest AI trend but is also about building the company.

TechCrunch Founder Summit 2026 takes place November 4 at SoWa Power Station in Boston.

items.title: Intel gets waiver after worries fuzzy US ban on foreign-made robots may hit fabs
items.summary: Company says foreign-made robotic vehicles are crucial to US chip production.
items.content:
US chip champion Intel was so confused by the US government ban on foreign-made robots that it requested and received a waiver “out of an abundance of caution.” The tech company wanted to make sure that it could continue using certain robotic vehicles in its US chip fabs.

The uncertainty surrounding the Federal Communications Commission ban on certain foreign-made robots was revealed in the agency’s decision to grant Intel’s waiver request. On October 22, the FCC published its order allowing Intel to continue using the foreign-made robots in US semiconductor manufacturing facilities for a period of one year.

The robots in question are automated guided vehicles operating on “tracks or predefined paths” while often requiring operator oversight, according to Intel’s website. They help to move materials and items around within warehouses and factory floors.

Such robotic vehicles are typically manufactured by Japanese companies like Murata Machinery and Daifuku Co., according to Bloomberg News . But the exact types of robotic vehicles used by Intel were only identified in a “confidential appendix” that accompanied its request.

The FCC’s ban mainly covers new models of mobile robots, like humanoid robots and robot vacuums, and still allows for the import of robots previously approved for sale in the United States. But the agency rules seem to restrict major modifications to “previously authorized devices.”

Intel’s waiver request stated that it was “unclear” whether its robotic vehicles even qualify as robots covered by the FCC ban but said it sought relief just in case. The tech company also received approval to “make certain hardware, software, and firmware changes” that would help ensure the continued operation and maintenance of the robotic vehicles.

The tech company described the robotic vehicles as being “critical to its domestic semiconductor manufacturing operations” and argued that the ability to maintain the robots was crucial to avoiding any disruptions to chip production. It also said there are no US-made alternatives that meet the company’s requirements.

The FCC approval came within a week of when Intel filed its waiver request on October 16. That is not too surprising given the importance of Intel to the Trump administration’s plans for reshoring chip manufacturing—not to mention that the US government took an $8.9 billion equity stake in the chip company.

Meanwhile, the US robotics industry at large is still grappling with the consequences of the FCC ban on foreign-made robots , given that China is the world’s leading supplier of robots and robotic components. Ars previously talked with one US robotics distributor that has pivoted from importing China’s humanoid robots to opening a US manufacturing facility for robots.

Some analysts have warned that the US government’s attempt to boost domestic production of robots via the restrictions on foreign-made robots could backfire for US industry. A report by the market intelligence firm International Data Corporation looks forward to 2030 and estimates that the FCC rule could reduce US revenue from deploying humanoid robots by 58 percent compared to pre-restriction expectations.

items.title: What’s the Best iPhone to Buy or Avoid Right Now? (2026)
items.summary: The first folding iPhone Duo is here, alongside the 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max, but they’re not your only options. We have all the details on Apple’s smartphone lineup to help you find the right model.
items.content:
Apple sells seven iPhone models, from the $699 iPhone 17e to the $1,999 iPhone Duo , but which iPhone is best for you? This is a good time of the year to buy an iPhone if you need to upgrade, since Apple just released its flagship models. (We don't expect the more affordable iPhone 18 models until spring 2027.) We've tested nearly every model and outlined their strengths and weaknesses so you can get the right one for you.

Check out our other Apple buying guides , including Which iPhone 18 Models to Buy , Which iPhone 17 Model to Buy , Best iPhone 17 Cases , Best MagSafe Accessories , Best MagSafe Chargers , Best MagSafe Wallets , and Best Apple 3-in-1 Chargers . Wondering what's new in iOS 27 ? We have details on that, too.

Updated October 2026: We’ve added more details on the iPhone Duo and links to our reviews and other related coverage now that it's available.

But First, Sell That Old iPhone!

If you’re upgrading from an iPhone, you can trade it in to Apple for a small discount. Before you do that, check whether you can sell it elsewhere for more money. iPhones hold their value incredibly well, particularly if they’re in mint or good condition. We have a guide that runs through the process of selling your phone, and we generally recommend you use websites like Swappa , Gazelle , or Back Market .

We also have a handful of setup guides you should follow:

Buying From Apple vs. a Carrier

Most people in the US purchase iPhones from carriers, which means the devices are locked to that network. If you bought an iPhone from Verizon, you can't easily switch to another carrier without breaking a contract and paying extra fees. It also poses headaches for travelers who want to use international SIM cards or eSIMs .

The easier approach is to buy directly from Apple, though there are some things you should know:

Connect to any carrier later: Choose this option for the most hassle-free experience. You get an unlocked iPhone, then all you need to do is transfer the SIM card or eSIM from your old iPhone to the new one to get started. This might be painless, though you may need to contact your carrier if the iPhone can't complete the eSIM transfer. In the US, Apple hasn't included a SIM tray since 2022's iPhone 14.

Choose a carrier: If you choose a carrier through Apple.com, you will get an unlocked iPhone, no matter which carrier you choose (except if you purchase with AT&T on an installment plan). The downside is that Apple doesn't have the same offers as the carriers, so you may lose out on a deal. However, carrier offers often require new lines, trade-ins, or an upgraded plan, and the savings come in the form of bill credits, so these deals aren't as amazing as they may seem.

Finance: You can finance your iPhone either with Apple's credit card via monthly installments or as Apple iPhone Payments via a Citizens One loan. You need to choose a carrier here, but Apple confirmed these devices are all unlocked. You have to fill out a credit application to see if you qualify. If you opt to finance through a carrier on Apple.com, only the T-Mobile and Verizon models will be unlocked. The AT&T and Boost Mobile options are locked iPhones, so it's no different from buying it on an installment plan directly from those carriers.

Apple Upgrade: Buying directly from Apple also nets you access to the Apple Upgrade leasing option. Is it worth it? Broadly speaking, no. Most people do not need to upgrade to a new iPhone every year or two. It's expensive, and you must return your leased iPhone in good condition to avoid additional charges. AppleCare is not included, as it was with the discontinued iPhone Upgrade Program .

What Is Apple Intelligence?

The most hyped-up feature from the iPhone 16 range was Apple Intelligence , which rolled out in iOS 18.1. This is Apple's suite of AI features, following the wave started by the likes of ChatGPT and Google's Gemini . Apple Intelligence is available on the iPhone 15 Pro/Pro Max and newer, including the iPhone 16e (not to mention select iPads and MacBooks ).

What exactly is Apple Intelligence in the first place? It's a collection of features that draw on the power of large language models to introduce “smart” capabilities. For example, in the Voice Memo and Notes app, you can now start a recording and get a real-time transcription. You can even record a call and get the transcription saved in the Notes app. Siri has been redesigned to understand when you misspeak and can even plug into ChatGPT for more powerful responses to open-ended questions. There are writing tools available throughout the operating system that let you change the tone of your emails or proofread text so you don't make an unnecessary typo on Threads.

This is just a small sampling. We've boiled down many of the Apple Intelligence features here , and additional features keep rolling out in iOS updates. For example, Genmoji —which lets you create your own emojis—debuted alongside the AI image-generation app, Image Playground, in iOS 18.2. In iOS 27, Apple added the revamped, conversational Siri AI assistant. Siri now understands personal context and can retrieve information from your messages, emails, and photos. It can also act on your behalf to draft a message with a particular tone or find a good restaurant for your partner's birthday dinner. Here's everything you can do with Siri AI .

If you don't care for Apple Intelligence and want to turn it off, you can! We have a helpful guide detailing the exact steps .

Magnetic MagSafe wireless charging is available on the iPhone 12, iPhone 13, iPhone 14, iPhone 15, iPhone 16, iPhone 17, and iPhone 18 models (except the iPhone 16e ), and it allows you to magnetically attach various accessories to the back of the iPhone. (iPhones support Qi2 , which is the open standard, whereas MagSafe is proprietary; you can use Qi2 accessories just like MagSafe.)

items.content:
We're introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro , the first model in our new K3.1 series and our most capable 3T-class open-weight model to date, with a 1-million-token context window. It delivers substantial improvements across coding, 3D creation, financial research, and other agentic capabilities.

We are also releasing Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed , which delivers 2-3× the speed of K3.1 Pro for more responsive interactions.

Kimi K3.1 Pro and Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed are available today on Kimi.ai , Kimi Work , Kimi Code , and the Kimi API . The full model weights will be released by Nov 4.

Kimi K3.1 Pro is a post-trained version of Kimi K3, with substantially larger post-training compute. To enable large-scale joint RL across hundreds of downstream domains , we optimized every layer of the stack — the RL framework, long-context inference, training efficiency, sandbox infrastructure, rollout scheduling, and a shared platform for environment quality checks — so that each increment of RL compute delivers stable, predictable returns. As a result, K3.1 Pro achieves consistent gains in every domain.

Across coding, agentic, and knowledge benchmarks, K3.1 Pro matches or approaches the strongest proprietary models. On Terminal-Bench 4.0 , which evaluates coding agents on realistic, resource-constrained terminal tasks using strict task-specific tests, K3.1 Pro scores 65.7%, ahead of GPT-6 Astra (58.2%) and narrowly behind Claude Opus 5.5 (66.4%) . And on Kimi Code Bench 3.0 Long-horizon , our internal benchmark that tests coding agents' multi-step execution, tool use, and end-to-end problem solving across diverse engineering domains, K3.1 Pro scores 61.2% , above K3's 55.95% .

K3.1 Pro covers the full range of coding work, from quick fixes in real codebases to full-project builds. It also brings a more considered visual style to games and web experiences, and knows how to build them with the right tools.

K3.1 Pro works effectively across game engines such as Unity, Unreal Engine, and Godot , combining them with web search and 3D generation to create complete experiences. Its front-end pages, interactive Three.js scenes, and 3D assets show stronger composition, typography, animation, and polish. The examples below were created end to end by K3.1 Pro:

K3.1 Pro's long-horizon coding capabilities are also strengthened through large-scale reinforcement learning. In one internal test, it built a human walking dynamics simulator with integrated training and evaluation pipelines on top of human-atlas , an open-source anatomical model of the human body comprising 296 skeletal components, including cartilage, and 402 muscle components. Across 167 missions and 420 independent reviews, it analyzed experimental results, diagnosed problems, and iteratively refined the walking controller, enabling the simulated human to go from collapsing within seconds to walking continuously with alternating strides for 11.2 seconds. When reward shaping failed to improve arm motion, K3.1 Pro did not simply keep adjusting the reward: it ran open-loop probes of the simulator's dynamics, identified and corrected 36 errors in shoulder-muscle moment-arm calculations, and then retrained the controller.

K3.1 Pro is strong at 3D creation and spatial reasoning. On BenchCAD , which tests 3D reconstruction from multi-view renderings through CAD code generation, K3.1 Pro scores 92.7% with tools , approaching the performance of Claude Opus 5.5 (96.2%) and GPT-6 Astra (95.9%) . From a text brief, sketch, or reference image, it can infer shape, proportions, and spatial relationships to create usable 3D models. It also has a stronger grasp of existing asset libraries and model collections.

K3.1 Pro particularly excels at parametric modeling, from mechanical parts and architectural models to configurable products and custom furniture. Without MCP connectors, it can write and run scripts for tools like Blender and CAD software to build and refine assets, edit components, and adjust geometry, materials, and scene layout.

With stronger reasoning and agentic capability, K3.1 Pro is capable of end-to-end delivery of complete financial workflows. K3.1 Pro achieves state-of-the-art results on OfficeQA Pro v2 (64.4), which tests complex fiscal data analysis over real financial documents through retrieval, cross-document verification, and multi-step numerical reasoning. K3.1 Pro also improves over K3 on Frontier Finance, which measures support for complete investment workflows from screening to profitability analysis.

K3.1 Pro also improves significantly across all our internal finance benchmarks:

Financial analysis and investment research demand a high degree of factual accuracy. To address this, we made targeted improvements to K3.1 Pro's factual accuracy on real-world tasks and challenging prompts. On Kimi Hallu Bench Hard bench, an internal benchmark designed to stress-test factual accuracy, its claim-level hallucination rate fell from 23.4% for K3 to 8.3%, while the share of responses containing at least one factual error was just 42.4% of its predecessor's rate. items.title: RFK Jr.’s vaccine injury clinic could damage NIH hospital, board warns
items.summary: "Trust is slow to build and quick to lose," board chair Jack Leslie said.
items.content:
At a recent meeting of the board that oversees the National Institutes of Health’s Clinical Center Research Hospital, chair Jack Leslie opened with cheerful introductions and gregarious chatter—then diverted from the agenda of the regularly scheduled meeting. He spent the next six minutes delivering a pointed rebuke of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, warning that his anti-vaccine activities could tarnish the venerable hospital, often called the “house of hope” for patients with rare conditions or those who have exhausted all other options.

Leslie took issue with a recent stunt Kennedy had pulled at the hospital, which involved making a surprise appearance for a ribbon-cutting ceremony to open his signature vaccine injury clinic . The ceremony included a panel with people claiming to have been injured by vaccines. They sat behind placards reading “vaccine injured” and spoke with Kennedy and other high-ranking Trump administration officials.

Leslie prefaced his comments by noting that some might prefer he not speak out against Kennedy’s efforts. “But I think that that would be a failing as an advisory board if we were silent,” he said. Leslie also noted that he has no concerns about studying potential injuries from vaccines. “Serious reactions are rare, but real,” he said, and people who believe they’ve been injured should “be taken seriously.”

In fact, the NIH already has a center that studies vaccine injuries, and Kennedy’s splashy new clinic does not come with more funding or clinic space. The hospital’s CEO, Jonathan Green , who sat next to Leslie at the meeting, chimed in to confirm that “the NIH has conducted research on the safety and efficacy of vaccines for decades in the past, and it ongoes.” Green described Kennedy’s vaccine injury clinic as merely a new, individual “protocol” for the hospital.

“The space in which this protocol will be conducted, the vaccine evaluation center inside the clinical center, has been in existence for decades,” Green said. Like all protocols, it needs to undergo rigorous scientific and ethical reviews before it’s implemented at the hospital. Green said the protocol is still under review.

None of this was made clear in Kennedy’s ceremony, and Leslie condemned the optics of the event, particularly the signs labeling patients “vaccine injured.” Those patients “must come first,” Leslie said. “They deserve our care and respect and they deserve answers.” But Kennedy does them—and the hospital—a disservice, Leslie argued.

“The secretary has spent two decades arguing that vaccines are dangerous,” Leslie said. “Those signs announce the conclusion that the research has not yet reached and that the research exists to test. Think about what that means for those patients. If this research finds evidence of harm, many will dismiss it as the work of a secretary who has long argued that vaccines are dangerous. If it finds none, patients will be told that the clinic was a sham. Either way, they’re left with answers no one trusts, and science only helps patients when the public believes it.”

Leslie said he feared that the stunt sends a political message that will undermine trust that the hospital has worked to earn and maintain for over 70 years.

“The clinical center standing rests on one thing: the confidence of patients, physicians, and the public that the research done here is designed to find the truth, not to confirm a conclusion reached in advance,” he said. “Trust is slow to build and quick to lose. If people come to believe that research at this hospital can be steered toward a politically desired answer, the damage will not stop at vaccines.”

After Leslie’s statement, another member thanked him and made a motion for the board to support the statement. The motion was quickly seconded and, in a voice vote, the board unanimously endorsed the comments.

items.title: Now Google says it might use your Gmail and Google Photos data to target ads
items.summary: Google has updated its privacy policy in a way that could mean you'll start seeing targeted ads based on your personal data if you're using personalized AI features. The update, spotted by Android Authority, adds an exception to its promise about not using your Drive, Gmail, or G
items.content:
According to the new terms, sharing your data for better AI recommendations also means opening it up for more personalized ads.

That means anyone who has connected their Drive, Gmail, or Google Photos to AI Mode and other Search tools via Google’s Personal Intelligence feature — allowing those tools to provide better responses or recommendations by knowing more about you — may now see ads targeted on the basis of that content.

Advertisers don’t get access to your Drive, Gmail, and Photos information or personally identifying details such as your name or email address, and Google won’t show you ads based on sensitive categories like race, sexual orientation, religion, or health.

This is what the policy says:

“You may choose to allow certain Google services, including services like Search or Gemini Apps, to access data from other Google services you use, such as Google Photos and Workspace apps like Gmail and Drive, in order to provide you with a more personalized experience, subject to the policies and settings of the accessing service. For example, Search may process some of the data that you allow Search to access to personalize content, including ads.”

“Depending on your settings, we may also show you personalized ads based on your interests, activity, or personalized content from Google services. For example, if you search for ‘mountain bikes,’ in Search you may see ads for sports equipment on YouTube.”

If you want to prevent your personal data from being used for targeted ads, you can choose which apps you want to disconnect from Search’s Personal Intelligence features or disable Personalized Recommendations entirely via the Search Services Personalization settings page.

items.title: Everybody panic: A Valve developer said "HLX" in public
items.summary: Sound designer lets Half Life-related codename slip at a conference.
items.content:
Gamers still hoping against hope for a true follow-up to Half-Life 2 (after so, so many years ) may remember last year’s flurry of speculation that Half-Life 3 was finally nearing completion . Amid all those rumors, though, we never got any official sign from anyone inside Valve that a Half-Life project was currently in development.

That changed this week thanks to an apparent slip-up during a panel at GameSoundCon , an industry conference devoted to “the art, technology, and business of game audio.” In a panel devoted to Valve’s use of open audio engines (captured in this Vimeo clip ), Valve composer and audio artist Mike Morasky let an interesting string of three letters slip while talking about the way the company implements high dynamic range (HDR) audio:

Our HDR system is basically that’s one of the three pieces that come together to make an HDR that you can easily optimize. And in fact, I think Deadlock has their own version of HDR. HLX has its own version , so on and so forth [emphasis added].

“HLX,” of course, has been widely reported as the internal code name for Valve’s next Half-Life project. The codename has shown up in Valve engine code since at least 2024 , but it has never been referenced in public by a Valve employee until now (though Morasky was responsible for a close call in an interview last year).

In the panel video, fellow panelist and Valve sound designer David Feise can be seen mumbling a sarcastic “nice work” to Morasky after the HLX codename slips out of his mouth. Later, while the audience is clapping at the end of the Q&A session, Feise leans in to Morasky and appears to say, “Good job—you only said HLX once!”

An official utterance of the “HLX” shibboleth is of course a good sign for those looking for any indication of the franchise continuing beyond 2020’s Half-Life Alyx . But the question of when Valve will make its next Half-Life project official still looms large.

Remember, it was just under a year ago that journalist Mike Straw was adamant that Half-Life 3 would be a Steam Machine launch title . Now that the Steam Machine launch has come and gone without even a nod toward an announcement, we can understand why Valve watchers would be more gun-shy than usual over any new rumors.

Longtime Valve watcher Tyler McVicker—who said Half-Life 3 was in the “final stages of development” and suggested a 2026 announcement was “likely” last year—admitted in a recent video that he now doesn’t believe that HLX is being announced this calendar year. But he also pointed to recently increased coding activity within Valve (as measured by externally viewable internal “commit” numbers) that something big might be coming sooner than later.

One thing is for sure: Whenever Half-Life 3 finally is announced and released, it will have to be truly incredible to make up for the loss of the long-running metagame of speculating about its mere existence .

items.content:
AI 활용해 공격 지능·정교화…실시간 탐지·엔드포인트 차단 강조

컴퓨팅 입력 :2026/10/24 01:26

김준영 에브리존 전략사업본부 총괄 팀장이 23일 "지금은 랜섬웨어에 감염되면 개인정보와 기밀 정보까지 유출된다고 봐야 한다"고 말했다. 랜섬웨어 피해를 방지하기 위해서는 방산 업체가 기술 유출과 업무 중단을 함께 막는 보안 체계를 갖춰야 한다고 제안했다.

김 팀장은 이날 방산기술보호·보안협의회가 주최한 '2026 AI기반 방산기술보호 컨퍼런스'에서 'AI 시대의 랜섬웨어: 탐지에서 차단과 복구로'를 주제로 발표했다.

에브리존은 한국인터넷진흥원(KISA) 자료를 인용해 국내 랜섬웨어 신고가 2024년 195건에서 2025년 274건으로 40.5% 늘었다고 소개했다. 그러면서 올해 신고 건수가 지난해를 크게 넘어설 것으로 내다봤다.

최근 랜섬웨어 피해 사례로는 SGI서울보증, 국내 제약사, 중소형 병원 등을 언급했다 . SGI서울보증은 4일간 업무가 중단돼 주요 보증 업무에 차질이 생겼다. 한 제약사는 2주간 전산 시스템 장애로 의약품 주문과 출고 시스템이 마비됐다. 중소 규모 병원 20곳은 동일한 랜섬웨어에 동시에 감염돼 진료에 차질을 빚었다. 지난달 상담한 고객사 한 곳에서만 감염이 동시에 50건 가까이 벌어졌다는 사례도 소개했다.

김 팀장은 방산 업체가 감염되면 연구 데이터가 암호화돼 개발 일정에 차질이 생긴다고 설명했다. 공장이 멈추면 무기 납품 일정도 어긋난다고 짚었다. 과거에는 암호화로 끝났지만 이제는 오랫동안 쌓은 연구개발 데이터가 외부로 유출될 수 있다고 강조했다.

9월 11일 시행된 개정 개인정보 보호법도 언급했다. 개인정보의 위조, 변조, 훼손도 유출 신고와 통지 대상에 포함돼 암호화만으로도 대응 부담이 커졌다는 설명이다.

랜섬웨어 침투 경로로는 ▲위장 이메일 첨부파일 실행 ▲외부에 노출된 원격접속 계정 탈취 ▲웹, 데이터베이스(DB) 서버 침투 등을 제시했다. 김 팀장은 "AI가 이들 경로를 통한 공격을 더 빠르고 정교하게 만든다"고 말했다.

특히 견적 요청서, 입사지원서, 세금계산서로 위장한 메일이 자연스러운 한국어는 물론 수신자의 말투까지 흉내 내고 있다고 짚었다. 생성형 AI 덕분에 악성코드 제작 시간이 수개월에서 수 시간으로 줄었다는 점도 언급했다.

그는 랜섬웨어를 만드는 조직과 퍼뜨리는 조직, 정보를 빼내는 조직이 나뉘어 있고 협상을 맡는 콜센터까지 운영한다고 전했다. 감염 피해자가 메일을 보내면 5분에서 10분 안에 답이 온다고 한다.

에브리존은 피해를 겪은 뒤 자사 제품을 도입한 국내 한 제약사 사례도 소개했다. 이 업체는 2022년 랜섬웨어에 감염돼 공장 가동이 한 달가량 멈췄다. 이후 백업 솔루션에 대규모로 투자했지만 이듬해 다시 감염됐다. 백업으로 데이터는 복구했지만 완료까지 약 7일이 걸렸고 업무 중단 등으로 150억원 가까운 손실이 났다. 해당 업체는 복구만으로는 부족하다고 보고 2023년 화이트디펜더를 도입했다.

그는 "백업은 복구를 가능하게 하지만 업무 중단과 손실까지 막지는 못한다"고 정리했다. 그러면서 랜섬웨어를 네트워크에서는 막을 수 없고 엔드포인트에서 막아야 한다고 말했다.

화이트디펜더는 악성코드 특징 정보(시그니처)에 의존하지 않고 파일 접근과 변경 행위를 분석해 암호화를 막는 행위 기반 제품이다. 자체 개발한 '트리플 디펜더 엔진'이 프로세스, 서비스, 커널 수준에서 암호화 시도를 탐지해 차단한다. '화이트 롤백 엔진'은 탐지 즉시 원본을 안전한 공간에 백업해 뒀다가 차단 뒤 복원한다. 에브리존은 기존 백신과 엔드포인트 탐지 및 대응(EDR) 솔루션과도 호환된다고 설명했다.

제품은 윈도 PC용, 윈도 서버용, 리눅스 서버용과 중앙관리 플랫폼으로 나뉜다. 국가정보원 보안기능확인서(2025년 3월)와 굿소프트웨어(GS) 인증 1등급(PC용 2018년, 윈도 서버용 2023년)을 획득했다. 누적 사용자는 96만6966명, 고객사는 2000곳 이상이다.

홍승균 에브리존 대표는 "랜섬웨어 공격에 당할 경우 모든 파일이 암호화되고, 데이터가 유출되며, 금전적인 피해로까지 이어진다"고 말했다. 이어 "업무 연속성이 중단되지 않도록 기업, 기관들이 대책을 강구해야 한다"고 말했다.

items.title: Agent cloud startup Daytona hits $1B valuation backed by FirstMark and a who’s who of angels
items.summary: Daytona is building a cloud for agents that's like giving every agent its own computer. It has attracted founders of Stripe, Perplextity, Datadog, Mercor, and others as angels, it says.
items.content:
Daytona Platforms announced on Friday that it had raised a $60 million Series B round at a $1 billion valuation led by FirstMark Growth. The company says it has now raised a total of $91 million.

The New York-based startup has attracted not just FirstMark (which also led its $24 million Series A in February), but also a host of well-known angels in this latest round. Daytona says they include Stripe’s Patrick Collison, Shopify’s Tobi Lütke, Perplexity’s Aravind Srinivas, Zoom’s Eric Yuan, Datadog’s Olivier Pomel, Quora’s Adam D’Angelo (who is also an OpenAI board member), and Mercor’s Brendan Foody. It also names Qualcomm Ventures, Samsung Next, and Okta Ventures as participants.

Three-year-old Daytona is building a cloud specifically for long-running agents, which have different infrastructure needs than yesteryear’s software, the startup contends. “Agents don’t work like the long-lived services today’s cloud was designed for. They spin up thousands of short, stateful jobs nobody planned in advance, and they need a cloud built for that,” founder Ivan Burazin wrote in a blog post announcing the new round . Daytona’s cloud, he said, is like giving every agent its own computer, where agents have access to sandboxed versions of Linux, Windows, macOS, and GPUs, among other services, on the one platform.

items.title: What some of Anthropic’s backers are worth before its IPO
items.summary: Early-stage and follow-on investors in the AI lab are already sitting on major paper returns.
items.content:
Anthropic’s public listing, which is expected this year at a valuation of as much as $2 trillion, is bound to be a windfall for both early-stage and later-stage investors. But even at the company’s latest private market valuation of $965 billion, the stakes held by many of those VCs and early backers already total billions.

Coatue , which first backed Anthropic in 2025 at a $183 billion valuation and co-led the AI lab’s last two funding rounds, has poured a total of $4.75 billion into the company. That stake, based on the last round’s price, is now worth roughly $7.5 billion, according to a person familiar with the matter. Coatue declined to comment.

Below is what some other backers of Anthropic are worth based on the last round’s price, according to Bloomberg :

Eric Schmidt: The former Google CEO invested in Anthropic’s Series A in 2021, when the startup was valued at $461 million, according to PitchBook data. Today, Schmidt owns about 1% of the company, and even at its current private valuation, his stake is worth nearly $10 billion.

Iconiq: The investment outfit wrote a $6 billion check to Anthropic last year when the company was already valued at $183 billion. That massive late-stage bet is now worth $17 billion and has the potential to double at the IPO.

Menlo Ventures: The VC firm led Anthropic’s Series D and has invested more than $1 billion in the company over time, a stake now worth $14 billion.

Sequoia: The famed VC firm backed the AI lab for the first time only earlier this year, when the company was already valued at $380 billion. The $3 billion investment gave it about 1% ownership, which means it has already more than doubled its investment.

Sound Ventures: The firm, launched by Guy Oseary and actor Ashton Kutcher, invested $35 million in Anthropic’s 2023 Series C round and has since funneled an additional $400 million into the company, resulting in a stake that’s worth billions now. (Kutcher left Sound Ventures this year to launch a new VC firm .)

Spark Capital: The only VC firm known to hold a board seat at Anthropic invested $75 million in that same 2023 Series C round, when it was valued at $5 billion. That position has ballooned more than ninetyfold to $7 billion.
